questions.question_text: Which single piece of information guarantees that a triangle is scalene?

options.text: All three of its angles are different sizes
Two of its angles are equal
options.why: Equal angles sit opposite equal sides, which makes the triangle isosceles.
A right-angled triangle can be isosceles as well as scalene, so this decides nothing.

options.text: All three of its angles are less than $90^{\circ}$
options.why: Being acute-angled says nothing about the sides; an equilateral triangle is acute.

questions.solution_text:
Equal angles sit opposite equal sides, so equal sides would force two equal angles.
If all three angles are different, no two sides can be equal.
All three angles being different sizes guarantees the triangle is scalene.

questions.question_text: Which of these triangles is impossible to draw?

options.text: A scalene triangle with two $50^{\circ}$ angles
A scalene triangle with a $90^{\circ}$ angle
options.why: Three sides of different lengths can still meet at an angle of $90^{\circ}$.

Two equal sides with every angle under $90^{\circ}$ is an ordinary isosceles triangle.

questions.solution_text:
Equal angles sit opposite equal sides.
Two angles of $50^{\circ}$ force the two sides opposite them to be equal.
A triangle with two equal sides is isosceles, not scalene, so this triangle is impossible.
